newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight business brisk, Brazil demand cited.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight business brisk, Brazil demand cited.

text.p: Business was brisk on London's sugar freight market on Wednesday although competition was noted from various operators looking for vessels to ply the same routes, shipbrokers said.
South Brazil's main sugar ports of Santos and Paranagua were predictably much in demand, they said.
Amerop quoted for 27/28,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Thailand to US Gulf/Atlantic or west coast for July 1/10.
Sugar Export was rumoured to be open for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos to Lagos for prompt shipment but shipbrokers said this was unconfirmed.
Both Cargill and E D & F Man issued new orders and were said to feature in the day's firmer business.
Cargill quoted for a 14,000-tonne bagged cargo on the same route required by Sugar Export, namely Santos to Lagos, for mid-June dates.
Cargill was also said to have fixed its recent order for 18,500 tonnes in bulk from Puerto Quetzal to Venezuela for prompt shipment.
E D & F Man entered the market with an enquiry for 7,500 tonnes of bagged sugar from two ports in north Spain to Dubai for prompt shipment, shipbrokers said.

Man fixed 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Santos to Dubai plus various options for prompt and a further 19,000 tonnes from Paranagua to Baltic/Black Sea for June 20/25. Details of the rates ahcieved have yet to emerge.
Lastly, Louis Dreyfus fixed 20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Durban to US Gulf/Atlantic for mid-June.
